findings.evidence: Line 139: `theorem subsingleton_filledHull_empty : (filledHull (∅ : Set E)).Subsingleton`; `Set.Subsingleton` gives "at most one element", not `= ∅`.
findings.fix: Rephrase to what the statement delivers, e.g. "says `filledHull ∅` is a subsingleton (it is in fact empty in a nontrivial space and a point in the zero space), so of diameter `0` either way" — or strengthen the lemma to the case split it is described as making.
findings.issue: The module docstring says `TauCeti.subsingleton_filledHull_empty` "says `filledHull ∅` is empty in a nontrivial space and a point in the zero space". The statement is only `(filledHull (∅ : Set E)).Subsingleton` (line 139); emptiness in a nontrivial space is established inside the proof but is not available to a reader who imports the lemma.

findings.evidence: Line 85 `theorem filledHull_subset_closedConvexHull (hK : K.Nonempty)`; line 84 of the same file states the containment fails without it (`filledHull ∅ = univ` in the zero space); proof line 166 dispatches `K = ∅` separately.
findings.fix: Qualify the sentence with the nonemptiness caveat and name the empty case, e.g. "for nonempty `K` the hull is contained in the closed convex hull …; `filledHull ∅` is a subsingleton".
findings.issue: `diam_filledHull`'s docstring asserts unconditionally that the hull "is contained in the closed convex hull of `K`", but `filledHull_subset_closedConvexHull` requires `K.Nonempty`, and the containment is false for `K = ∅` in the zero space — the case the same file stresses elsewhere and which the proof handles via `subsingleton_filledHull_empty`.

summary: Module and declaration docstrings are thorough and their cross-references (winding lemmas, DiamFrontier, SmallJordanCurve, roadmap L5/STATUS) all check out; two explanatory sentences attribute more to a declaration than its statement delivers.
